cards.title: Word Formation, Affixes
rule: Definition: Word Formation and Derivational Morphology (ስነ-ቅርጺ ቃላትን ምምስራት ሓደሽቲ ቃላትን) refers to the processes of creating new words from existing root words by adding prefixes and suffixes, thereby modifying their semantic meaning or converting them into different grammatical word classes.

English word formation is heavily dependent on concatenative morphology, where prefixes (added to the beginning of a root) and suffixes (added to the end of a root) are sequentially attached to a base form ($$\text{Prefix} + \text{Root} + \text{Suffix}$$). In contrast, Tigrinya uses a Semitic root-and-pattern (consonantal root) system. In Tigrinya, word class conversion and nominalization are primarily achieved through internal vowel melody shifts and consonant doubling within a triconsonantal root (e.g., the root {s-b-r} meaning 'to break' produces "ስባር" [broken piece] or "ስባረ" [fracture]) rather than the linear affixation typical of English. This fundamental morphological difference is a major conceptual hurdle for Tigrinya-speaking students, who must transition from an internal consonantal modification system to a linear, suffix-based word-building system.

cards.title: Notes
body: Definition: Word Formation and Derivational Morphology (ስነ-ቅርጺ ቃላትን ምምስራት ሓደሽቲ ቃላትን) refers to the processes of creating new words from existing root words by adding prefixes and suffixes, thereby modifying their semantic meaning or converting them into different grammatical word classes.

English word formation is heavily dependent on concatenative morphology, where prefixes (added to the beginning of a root) and suffixes (added to the end of a root) are sequentially attached to a base form ($$\text{Prefix} + \text{Root} + \text{Suffix}$$). In contrast, Tigrinya uses a Semitic root-and-pattern (consonantal root) system. In Tigrinya, word class conversion and nominalization are primarily achieved through internal vowel melody shifts and consonant doubling within a triconsonantal root (e.g., the root {s-b-r} meaning 'to break' produces "ስባር" [broken piece] or "ስባረ" [fracture]) rather than the linear affixation typical of English. This fundamental morphological difference is a major conceptual hurdle for Tigrinya-speaking students, who must transition from an internal consonantal modification system to a linear, suffix-based word-building system.

Nominalization (ምስራሕ ስማት) is the process of converting verbs or adjectives into nouns. Verbs are converted to nouns using suffixes like *-ment, -tion, -sion, -ance, -ence, -al* ($$\text{Verb} + \text{Suffix} \rightarrow \text{Noun}$$, e.g., *agree* $$\rightarrow$$ *agreement*, *decide* $$\rightarrow$$ *decision*, *assist* $$\rightarrow$$ *assistance*). Adjectives are converted to nouns using suffixes like *-ness, -ity, -dom, -hood, -ship* ($$\text{Adjective} + \text{Suffix} \rightarrow \text{Noun}$$, e.g., *happy* $$\rightarrow$$ *happiness*, *pure* $$\rightarrow$$ *purity*, *free* $$\rightarrow$$ *freedom*). National examinations frequently test these nominalized forms in subject and object slots, requiring students to identify spelling adjustments (e.g., dropping 'y' to 'i' in *happiness* or consonant shifts in *decide* $$\rightarrow$$ *decision*).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The sudden ________ of the school principal surprised both the teachers and the students.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The blank follows the article 'The' and the adjective 'sudden', requiring a noun ($$\text{Article} + \text{Adjective} + \text{Noun}$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often choose the verb 'depart' (Option A) due to direct translation. Only the nominalized form 'departure' (Option B), formed by adding the suffix '-ure' to the verb 'depart', is grammatically correct.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
እቲ ባዶ ቦታ ድሕሪ 'The' (ኣንቀጽ) ከምኡ ውን ድሕሪ 'sudden' (ቅጽል) ስለ ዝመጸ፡ ብግድን ስም (noun) ክኸውን ኣለዎ። እቲ 'depart' (ምኻድ) ዝብል ግሲ ናብ ስም ክቕየር ከሎ ድማ 'departure' (Option B - ምኻድ/ምስጓም) ይኸውን። 'depart' ምጥቃም ሰዋስዋዊ ጌጋ እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The instructions provided by the examiner were highly ________, which caused many candidates to make mistakes.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The context 'which caused many candidates to make mistakes' indicates a negative adjective is required to describe the instructions.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often struggle with negative prefixes and choose 'disclear' (Option C) or 'inclear' (Option D). The correct negative prefix for the adjective 'clear' is 'un-', forming 'unclear' (Option B).

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
ተመሃሮ ጌጋ ከም ዝገበሩ ስለ ዝገለጸ፡ እቲ መግለጺ 'ዘይነጸረ' (negative adjective) ክኸውን ኣለዎ። ኣብ እንግሊዘኛ ን 'clear' (ንጹር) ኣሉታዊ ክንገብሮ ከለና እንጥቅመሉ ቅድመ-መጣበቕታ 'un-' ስለ ዝኾነ፡ ቅኑዕ መልሲ 'unclear' (Option B - ዘይንጹር) እዩ።
